EXT_G5_FP_2016_025.q: Mister Sam's age in the year 2000 was a multiple of 8, and in the year 2001 it was a multiple of 7. In which year was Mister Sam born?

steps: Let E equal f minus 9, which is even.
The 25th odd number after E is E plus 1, plus 24 times 2. That equals E plus 49.

EXT_G5_FP_2018_005.q: A palindrome number is a number which remains the same when read backwards. For example, 707 or 5225. A three-digit palindrome number is added to 2017, to get a 4-digit palindrome number. What is the sum of the digits of the three-digit palindrome number added to 2017?

B equals 3 gives 2552, which reads the same backwards. So the number is 535.

EXT_G5_FP_2020_037.q: Jack is reading a book whose pages are numbered from 1. The page numbers of the book have a total of 555 digits. How many pages are there in Jack's book?

Before an odd number, call it O, the nth even number is O minus 1, minus, open bracket, n minus 1, close bracket, times 2.
steps: Let O equal M plus 46, which is odd.
The 19th even number before O is O minus 1, minus 18 times 2. That equals O minus 37.
That is M plus 46, minus 37, which equals M plus 9.

EXT_G5_FP_2023_012.q: What is the product of all the one-digit factors of 48?
hints: List the factors of 48 that are less than 10, then multiply them all.
The factors of 48 below 10 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 8.
steps: Check 1 to 9. 1, yes. 2, yes. 3, yes. 4, yes. 5, no. 6, yes. 7, no. 8, yes. 9, no.
The product is 1 times 2 times 3 times 4 times 6 times 8.
That is 24 times 48, which equals 1152.

EXT_G5_FP_2023_027.q: What will be the place value of the digit 6, in the product of the greatest two-digit prime number and the greatest three-digit number?
hints: The greatest two-digit prime is 97, and the greatest three-digit number is 999. Multiply them, using 97 times 1000, minus 97. Then find where the 6 sits.
97 times 999 equals 97 times 1000, minus 97.
steps: 97 times 999 is 97000 minus 97, which equals 96903.
In 96903, the digit 6 is in the thousands place.
The place value is 6000.

EXT_G5_FP_2023_034.q: Form the smallest 5-digit even number using the digits 7, 4, 3, 6 and 9, each only once, and state which digit will come in the hundreds place.
hints: An even number must end in 4 or 6. Try both: put the smallest digits at the front of each, then compare the two numbers.
For the smallest number, put the smallest digits first, but the last digit must be even.
steps: Ending in 4, the remaining digits are 3, 6, 7 and 9. That gives 36794.
Ending in 6, the remaining digits are 3, 4, 7 and 9. That gives 34796.
The smaller one is 34796.
The digit in the hundreds place, which is 3rd from the left in 34796, is 7.

EXT_G5_FP_2024_007.q: Find the sum of the seventh consecutive odd number coming after 54, and the 12th consecutive even number coming before 65.
hints: Write the odd numbers that come after 54, starting at 55, and the even numbers that come before 65, counting backwards from 64.
Odd numbers and even numbers both go up or down in jumps of 2.
steps: The odd numbers after 54 are 55, 57, 59, 61, 63, 65, 67. So the 7th is 67.
The even numbers before 65, counting back, are 64, 62, 60, and so on. The 12th is 64, minus 11 times 2, which equals 42.
The sum is 67 plus 42, which equals 109.

EXT_G5_FP_2024_011.q: What is the place value of the digit 4, in the square of the greatest two-digit prime number?
hints: For the greatest two-digit prime, check 99, 98, 97, and so on. Then square it, and see which place the digit 4 sits in.
Place value equals the digit, times the value of its place. For hundreds, that is times 100.
steps: 99 equals 9 times 11, so no. 98 is even, so no. 97 is prime, yes.
97 squared is 97 times 97, which equals 9409.
In 9409, the digit 4 is in the hundreds place. So 4 times 100 equals 400.

EXT_G5_FP_2024_025.q: How many two-digit prime numbers are there, whose sum of digits is more than 10?
hints: A prime has only 1 and itself as factors. First list all the two-digit primes, then add the digits of each one. More than 10 means 11 or higher.
steps: Add the digits of each prime. Keep only the sums that are 11 or more.
29 gives 11. 47 gives 11. 59 gives 14. 67 gives 13. 79 gives 16. 83 gives 11. 89 gives 17. 97 gives 16. All of these count.
Careful: 19, 37 and 73 have a digit sum of exactly 10, which is not more than 10.
The count is 8.

EXT_G5_FP_2024_039.q: What is the sum of all one-digit factors of 72?
hints: List the factors of 72 in pairs: 1 times 72, 2 times 36, and so on. Then pick only the ones below 10.
The factor pairs of 72 are 1 times 72, 2 times 36, 3 times 24, 4 times 18, 6 times 12, and 8 times 9.
steps: All the factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36 and 72.
The one-digit factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 9.
The sum is 1 plus 2 plus 3 plus 4 plus 6 plus 8 plus 9, which equals 33.

EXT_G5_FP_2025_001.q: If you add all one-digit odd numbers, and multiply the sum by the greatest two-digit prime number, what would be the place value of the digit in the hundreds place?
hints: One-digit odd numbers are 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9. Add them, then multiply by the greatest two-digit prime. It is more than 90.
The hundreds place is the 3rd digit from the right.
steps: The sum is 1 plus 3 plus 5 plus 7 plus 9, which equals 25.
The greatest two-digit prime is 97.
25 times 97 equals 2425.
The digit in the hundreds place is 4. So the place value is 400.

EXT_G5_FP_2025_015.q: Find the sum of the 12th even number serially coming after 99, and the 18th even number serially coming before 99.
hints: The first even number after 99 is 100. The first even number before 99 is 98. Then count in 2s.
The nth even number after 99 is 100, plus, open bracket, n minus 1, close bracket, times 2. The nth even number before 99 is 98, minus, open bracket, n minus 1, close bracket, times 2.
steps: The 12th even number after 99 is 100, plus 11 times 2. That is 100 plus 22, which equals 122.
The 18th even number before 99 is 98, minus 17 times 2. That is 98 minus 34, which equals 64.
The sum is 122 plus 64, which equals 186.

EXT_G5_WS_01_001.q: How many tens form six hundred hundreds?
hints: First figure out what six hundred hundreds means as a single number.
Six hundred hundreds is 600 times 100, which is 60,000. Now divide by 10 to find how many tens.
A simpler example: how many tens in two hundred? 200 divided by 10 equals 20 tens. Now do 60,000 divided by 10.
steps: Find the value of six hundred hundreds.
Divide by 10 to convert to tens.

EXT_G5_WS_01_002.q: Which of the following digits has the same place value and face value, irrespective of the place it is in?
hints: Face value is the digit itself. Place value is the digit times the worth of its place: 1, 10, 100, and so on. When could these two be equal in every place?
Test each choice in the tens place. 9 in the tens place is worth 9 times 10, which is 90, and that is not 9. Now test the other digits the same way.

Here is how to test a digit. 4 in the hundreds place has face value 4, but place value 4 times 100, which is 400. They differ, so 4 does not work. Look for a digit that stays the same when multiplied by 10 or 100.
steps: Face value is the digit itself. Place value equals the digit, times the position value.
For 0: 0 times any position is 0. The face value is 0. They always match.
So 0 always has the same place value and face value.

EXT_G5_WS_01_003.q: If the place value of a digit is an odd number, which place is that digit in?
hints: Place value is the digit times 1, 10, 100 or 1000, depending on its place. Think about which of these products can ever be odd.
Multiply any digit by 10: the result ends in 0, so it is even. Check what happens with 1000, and with 1, in the same way.

An example: 5 in the hundreds place is worth 5 times 100, which is 500. That is even, even though 5 is odd. So the hundreds place can never give an odd place value. Test the places in the choices like this.
steps: The place value in the tens place is the digit times 10, which is always even.
The place value in the hundreds or thousands place is the digit times 100 or 1000, which is always even.
The place value in the units place is the digit times 1, which is the digit itself. This can be odd.
Only the units place can produce an odd place value.

EXT_G5_WS_01_004.q: In the number 69512, what is the difference between the digits that have the greatest and the least place values?
hints: Identify which digit is in the highest place, the ten-thousands, and which is in the lowest, the units.
In 69512, the digit in the ten-thousands place is 6, and the digit in the units place is 2.
A simpler example: in 853, the digit in the hundreds place, the highest, is 8. The digit in the units place, the lowest, is 3. The difference is 8 minus 3, which is 5.
steps: The digit in the greatest place, the ten-thousands, is 6.
The digit in the least place, the units, is 2.
Find the difference: 6 minus 2 equals 4.

EXT_G5_WS_01_005.q: In the number 76025, how many times is the place value of 6 to that of 2?
hints: Find the place value of 6, and the place value of 2, in 76025. How many times, means you divide the bigger place value by the smaller one.
6 is in the thousands place, so it is worth 6000. 2 is in the tens place, so it is worth 20. Now divide 6000 by 20.
An example: in 8040, the 8 is worth 8000, and the 4 is worth 40. 8000 divided by 40 equals 200. So the place value of 8 is 200 times that of 4.
steps: The place value of 6, in the thousands place: 6 times 1000 equals 6000.
The place value of 2, in the tens place: 2 times 10 equals 20.
Divide: 6000 divided by 20 equals 300.

EXT_G5_WS_01_006.q: The digit 8 is used twice in each of the following numbers. In which number is the place value of one 8, a thousand times that of the other 8?
hints: Each step to the left makes a digit worth 10 times more. So for one 8 to be worth 1000 times the other, how many places apart must the two 8s be?
1000 equals 10 times 10 times 10, so the two 8s must be three places apart, like units and thousands, or tens and ten-thousands. In each number, find the places of the two 8s.
An example: in 5052, one 5 is worth 5000, and the other is worth 50. 5000 divided by 50 equals 100, so one is only 100 times the other. Two places apart gives 100 times. You need three places apart.
steps: Check 68815. The 8s are in the thousands place, worth 8000, and the hundreds place, worth 800. 8000 divided by 800 is 10, not 1000.
Check 65818. The 8s are in the hundreds place, worth 800, and the units place, worth 8. 800 divided by 8 is 100, not 1000.
Check 81586. The 8s are in the ten-thousands place, worth 80000, and the tens place, worth 80. 80000 divided by 80 is 1000. That works.
This is the one where one 8 is 1000 times the other: 81586.

EXT_G5_WS_01_007.q: In which of the following is the place value of one 3, a hundred times that of the other 3 in the same number?
hints: Each step to the left makes a digit worth 10 times more. For one 3 to be worth 100 times the other, how many places apart must the two 3s be?
100 equals 10 times 10, so the two 3s must be two places apart, like tens and thousands. In each number, write down the places of the two 3s.
An example: in 7479, one 7 is worth 7000, and the other is worth 70. 7000 divided by 70 equals 100, so one 7 is 100 times the other. Look for the number where the 3s sit like this.
steps: For one 3 to be worth 100 times the other, the two 3s must be two places apart, because 10 times 10 equals 100.
In 134639 the 3s are worth 30000 and 30. 30000 divided by 30 equals 1000, so this is not a match. In 752339 they are worth 300 and 30. 300 divided by 30 equals 10, not a match.
In 307638 the 3s are worth 300000 and 30. 300000 divided by 30 equals 10000, not a match.
In 863135 the 3s are worth 3000 and 30. 3000 divided by 30 equals 100. So the number is 863135.

EXT_G5_WS_01_011.q: What is the successor of the greatest four-digit number formed by using the digits 1, 5, 0 and 8, each only once?
hints: First, form the greatest four-digit number using 1, 5, 0 and 8, each once.
To make the greatest number, arrange the digits in descending order: 8, 5, 1, 0. That gives 8510.
Try this: the greatest 3-digit number with 3, 7 and 1 is 731. Its successor is 732.
steps: Arrange the digits in descending order for the greatest number: 8, 5, 1, 0. That gives 8510.
Find the successor, by adding 1: 8510 plus 1 equals 8511.

EXT_G5_WS_01_012.q: Which digit is exactly in the middle of the greatest odd number formed by using the digits 5, 8, 0, 7 and 4, each only once?
hints: An odd number ends in an odd digit. Which of the digits 5, 8, 0, 7 and 4 are odd? One of them must go in the units place.

To make the number as big as possible, put the biggest digits on the left. Try both ways. End with 5, and arrange 8, 7, 4, 0 from biggest to smallest. Then end with 7, and arrange 8, 5, 4, 0. Which number is greater?
An example with 1, 6, 3: the greatest odd number ends in 1 or 3. Ending in 1 gives 631. Ending in 3 gives 613. 631 is greater, and its middle digit is 3.
steps: The greatest odd number must end in an odd digit, 5 or 7.
Try ending in 5. The remaining digits, 8, 7, 4, 0, in descending order, give 87405.
Try ending in 7. The remaining digits, 8, 5, 4, 0, in descending order, give 85407.
87405 is greater than 85407, so the greatest odd number is 87405.
The middle digit, the 3rd, of 87405 is 4.

EXT_G5_WS_01_013.q: What is the place value of 7, in the smallest even number formed by using the digits 2, 7, 3, 9 and 6, each only once?
hints: An even number ends in an even digit. Which of the digits 2, 7, 3, 9 and 6 are even? One of them must go in the units place.

To make the number as small as possible, put the smallest digits on the left. Try both ways. End with 2, and arrange 3, 6, 7, 9 from smallest to biggest. Then end with 6, and arrange 2, 3, 7, 9. Which number is smaller, and where is the 7?
An example with 1, 4, 5: the smallest even number must end in 4, so it is 154. The 5 is in the tens place, so its place value is 5 times 10, which is 50.
steps: The smallest even number must end in an even digit: 2 or 6.
Ending in 2, arrange the rest in ascending order. That gives 36792.
Ending in 6, arrange the rest in ascending order. That gives 23796.
23796 is less than 36792, so the smallest even number is 23796.
7 is in the hundreds place. Its place value is 700.

EXT_G5_WS_01_014.q: How many two-digit even numbers have an odd digit in the tens place?
hints: Two-digit even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. That is 5 choices. The tens digit must be odd.
The odd digits for the tens place are 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. That is 5 choices. The even digits for the units place are 0, 2, 4, 6, 8. That is 5 choices.
Try this: how many two-digit numbers have 1 in the tens place, and are even? 10, 12, 14, 16, 18. That is 5 numbers.
steps: The odd digits for the tens place are 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. That is 5 choices.
The even digits for the units place are 0, 2, 4, 6, 8. That is 5 choices.
The total is 5 times 5. And 5 times 5 equals 25.

EXT_G5_WS_01_015.q: Using the digits 7, 0, 3 and 9, each only once, how many distinct four-digit numbers can be formed?
hints: A four-digit number cannot begin with 0. So think about which digits are allowed in the thousands place.
The thousands place can be 7, 3 or 9: that is 3 choices. After that, count how many ways the other three digits can fill the remaining three places.
An example with 1, 0, 2: a three-digit number can start with 1 or 2. That is 2 choices. The other two digits can then be placed in 2 ways. 2 times 2 equals 4 numbers: 102, 120, 201 and 210.
steps: The thousands place cannot be 0, so it can be 7, 3 or 9. That is 3 choices.
The 3 digits left over fill the other three places: 3 choices for the hundreds, then 2 for the tens, then 1 for the units. 3 times 2 times 1 equals 6 ways.
Multiply the choices: 3 times 6 equals 18. So 18 different four-digit numbers can be formed.

EXT_G5_WS_01_016.q: How many four-digit numbers less than 5000 can be formed using the digits 2, 5, 0 and 8, each only once?
hints: A number less than 5000 must have a thousands digit smaller than 5. And a four-digit number cannot begin with 0.
From 2, 5, 0 and 8, only 2 can go in the thousands place. Now count the ways to arrange 5, 0 and 8 in the other three places.
An example: numbers less than 300, using 1, 4, 6 once each, must start with 1. Then 4 and 6 can go in 2 ways: 146 and 164. So there are 2 such numbers.
steps: A number less than 5000 needs a thousands digit below 5, and it cannot be 0. From 2, 5, 0 and 8, only 2 works.
The digits 5, 0 and 8 fill the other three places: 3 choices for the hundreds, then 2 for the tens, then 1 for the units. 3 times 2 times 1 equals 6 ways.
So 6 four-digit numbers less than 5000 can be formed: 2058, 2085, 2508, 2580, 2805 and 2850.

EXT_G5_WS_B2_011.q: If the digits 5 and 6 are interchanged in the number 469571, by how much is the new number more than, or less than, the original number?
hints: Find the digits 5 and 6 in 469571, and say which place each one is in. Then swap them, and compare the new number with the old one.
The 6 is in the ten-thousands place, and the 5 is in the hundreds place. After the swap, the new number is 459671. Is that bigger or smaller than 469571, and by how much?
A similar one: swap 2 and 7 in 1274, to get 1724. The new number is more, by 1724 minus 1274, which is 450.
steps: In 469571 the digit 6 is in the ten-thousands place, and the digit 5 is in the hundreds place.
Swap them: the new number is 459671.
The ten-thousands digit went down from 6 to 5, so the new number is smaller than the original.
Subtract to find by how much: 469571 minus 459671 equals 9900. So the new number is less by 9900.

EXT_G5_WS_B3_010.q: In a bundle of notes of 5 rupees denomination, the notes are numbered serially from 40801 to 40901. What is the total amount of money in this bundle?
hints: How many notes are there from 40801 to 40901?
The count is 40901 minus 40801, plus 1, which is 101 notes. The total is 101 times 5.
Try this: notes from 1 to 5 make 5 notes. 5 times 5 rupees equals 25 rupees.
steps: Count the notes from 40801 to 40901. Subtract and add 1, because both the first and the last note are counted. 40901 minus 40801, plus 1, equals 101 notes.
Each note is worth 5 rupees, so multiply: 101 times 5 equals 505.
So the bundle holds 505 rupees in all.

EXT_G5_WS_B4_018.q: In writing all the prime numbers from 1 to 100, how many times is the digit 7 used?
hints: Write out all the prime numbers from 1 to 100. Then go through your list and tick every 7 you see, in the tens place or the ones place.
Do it in two parts. First, the primes that end in 7, starting 7, 17, 37, and so on. Then the primes that begin with 7, in the seventies. Careful: 27, 57, 77 and 87 are not prime.
Try a smaller one: the digit 3 in the primes up to 50. Ending in 3: 3, 13, 23, 43. Starting with 3: 31, 37. That is 6 threes.
steps: The primes containing the digit 7 are 7, 17, 37, 47, 67, 71, 73, 79 and 97.
Each contains exactly one 7. No prime has two 7s, since 77 equals 7 times 11.
The total count of the digit 7 is 9.

EXT_G5_WS_B4_019.q: How many times is the digit 3 used in writing all the two-digit prime numbers?
hints: List all the two-digit primes, then count the digit 3 in each.
A similar example: count the digit 1 in two-digit primes: 11, which has two 1s, then 13, 17, 19, 31, 41, 61, 71. The count is 2 plus 1 plus 1 plus 1 plus 1 plus 1 plus 1 plus 1, which equals 9.
steps: The two-digit primes with the digit 3 are 13, 23, 31, 37, 43, 53, 73 and 83.
Count the 3s: each has exactly one 3. 33 is not prime.
The total is 8.

EXT_G5_WS_B4_020.q: Using all the one-digit prime numbers, each only once, how many even numbers can be formed?
hints: The one-digit primes are 2, 3, 5 and 7. An even number must end in an even digit. Which of these four digits is even?
The digit 2 has to go in the ones place. Now arrange 3, 5 and 7 in the other three places. List them in order: 3572, 3752, and so on, and count.
Try a smaller one: using 2, 3 and 5 once each, the even numbers must end in 2. They are 352 and 532, so there are 2.
steps: The one-digit primes are 2, 3, 5 and 7. All four digits are used, so each number has four digits.
An even number ends in an even digit, and 2 is the only even one. So 2 goes in the ones place.
The digits 3, 5 and 7 fill the other three places: 3572, 3752, 5372, 5732, 7352 and 7532.
So 6 even numbers can be formed.

PH3_EXT_G5_WS_01_001_01.q: How many numbers from 1 to 201 are divisible by 8?
hints: Find the first and last multiples of 8 in the range.
The first is 8, and the last is 200.
The count is last minus first, divided by 8, plus 1.
steps: The first multiple of 8, from 1 onwards, is 8.
The last multiple of 8, up to 201, is 200.
The count is 200 minus 8, divided by 8, plus 1. That equals 25.

PH3_EXT_G5_WS_01_001_02.q: A book has 50 pages. How many digits are used to number all the pages?
hints: Pages 1 to 9 use 1 digit each, pages 10 to 99 use 2 digits each, and pages from 100 onwards use 3 digits each.
Count each group separately and add.
There are 9 single-digit pages.
steps: Pages 1 to 9: that is 9 pages, times 1 digit, which is 9 digits.
Pages 10 to 50: that is 41 pages, times 2 digits, which is 82.
The total is 91 digits.

PH3_EXT_G5_WS_01_001_03.q: How many 3-digit even numbers are there?
hints: The smallest 3-digit number is 100 and the largest is 999. Count all of them first, then think about how many are even.
Count them all: 999 minus 100, plus 1. Then remember that even and odd numbers take turns.
Even and odd numbers alternate, so here exactly half are even. Try a smaller one: from 10 to 19 there are 10 numbers, and 5 of them are even.
steps: The smallest 3-digit number is 100 and the largest is 999.
Count them all, counting both ends. 999 minus 100, plus 1, equals 900.
Even and odd numbers alternate. The list starts with an even number and ends with an odd number, so exactly half are even. 900 divided by 2 equals 450.
So there are 450 3-digit even numbers.

PH3_EXT_G5_WS_01_003_01.q: How many numbers from 50 to 100 are divisible by 6?
hints: Find the first and last multiples of 6 in the range.
The first is 54, and the last is 96.
The count is last minus first, divided by 6, plus 1.
steps: The first multiple of 6, from 50 onwards, is 54.
The last multiple of 6, up to 100, is 96.
The count is 96 minus 54, divided by 6, plus 1. That equals 8.

PH3_EXT_G5_WS_01_003_02.q: A book has 100 pages. How many digits are used to number all the pages?
hints: Pages 1 to 9 use 1 digit each, pages 10 to 99 use 2 digits each, and pages from 100 onwards use 3 digits each.
Count each group separately and add.
There are 9 single-digit pages.
steps: Pages 1 to 9: that is 9 pages with 1 digit each. So 9 times 1 equals 9 digits.
Pages 10 to 99: that is 90 pages with 2 digits each. So 90 times 2 equals 180 digits.
Page 100 is the only page with 3 digits, so it uses 3 digits.
Add them up: 9 plus 180 plus 3 equals 192. So 192 digits are used.

PH3_EXT_G5_WS_01_003_03.q: How many 3-digit numbers are there in all?
hints: The smallest 3-digit number is 100 and the largest is 999. You need to count every number from one to the other.
To count from 100 to 999, subtract and then add 1, so that both ends are counted. That is 999 minus 100, plus 1.
Try a smaller one. From 5 to 9 there are 9 minus 5, plus 1, which is 5 numbers. Count them to check: 5, 6, 7, 8, 9.
steps: The smallest 3-digit number is 100 and the largest is 999.
Count from 100 to 999, counting both ends. 999 minus 100, plus 1, equals 900.
So there are 900 3-digit numbers in all.

PH3_EXT_G5_WS_01_012_01.q: How many numbers from 100 to 300 are divisible by 5?
hints: Find the first and last multiples of 5 in the range.
The first is 100, and the last is 300.
The count is last minus first, divided by 5, plus 1.
steps: The first multiple of 5, from 100 onwards, is 100.
The last multiple of 5, up to 300, is 300.
The count is 300 minus 100, divided by 5, plus 1. That equals 41.

PH3_EXT_G5_WS_01_012_02.q: A book has 150 pages. How many digits are used to number all the pages?
hints: Pages 1 to 9 use 1 digit each, pages 10 to 99 use 2 digits each, and pages from 100 onwards use 3 digits each.
Count each group separately and add.
There are 9 single-digit pages.
steps: Pages 1 to 9: that is 9 pages, times 1 digit, which is 9 digits.
Pages 10 to 99: that is 90 pages, times 2 digits, which is 180.
Pages 100 to 150: that is 51 pages, times 3 digits, which is 153.
The total is 342 digits.

PH3_EXT_G5_WS_01_012_03.q: How many 2-digit even numbers are there?
hints: The smallest 2-digit number is 10 and the largest is 99. Count all of them first, then think about how many are even.
Count them all: 99 minus 10, plus 1. Then remember that even and odd numbers take turns.
Even and odd numbers alternate, so here exactly half are even. Try a smaller one: from 10 to 19 there are 10 numbers, and 5 of them are even.
steps: The smallest 2-digit number is 10 and the largest is 99.
Count them all, counting both ends. 99 minus 10, plus 1, equals 90.
Even and odd numbers alternate. The list starts with an even number and ends with an odd number, so exactly half are even. 90 divided by 2 equals 45.
So there are 45 2-digit even numbers.

PH3_EXT_G5_WS_01_014_01.q: How many numbers from 10 to 210 are divisible by 9?
hints: Find the first and last multiples of 9 in the range.
The first is 18, and the last is 207.
The count is last minus first, divided by 9, plus 1.
steps: The first multiple of 9, from 10 onwards, is 18.
The last multiple of 9, up to 210, is 207.
The count is 207 minus 18, divided by 9, plus 1. That equals 22.

PH3_EXT_G5_WS_01_014_02.q: A book has 200 pages. How many digits are used to number all the pages?
hints: Pages 1 to 9 use 1 digit each, pages 10 to 99 use 2 digits each, and pages from 100 onwards use 3 digits each.
Count each group separately and add.
There are 9 single-digit pages.
steps: Pages 1 to 9: that is 9 pages, times 1 digit, which is 9 digits.
Pages 10 to 99: that is 90 pages, times 2 digits, which is 180.
Pages 100 to 200: that is 101 pages, times 3 digits, which is 303.
The total is 492 digits.

PH3_EXT_G5_WS_01_014_03_b.q: How many odd numbers are there from 100 to 140?
hints: Find the first and last odd number in the range.
Use the formula: last minus first, divided by 2, plus 1.
The first odd number in the range is 101, and the last is 139.
steps: The first odd number is 101, and the last odd number is 139.
The count is 139 minus 101, divided by 2, plus 1. That equals 20.

PH3_EXT_G5_WS_01_015_01.q: How many numbers from 1 to 101 are divisible by 8?
hints: Find the first and last multiples of 8 in the range.
The first is 8, and the last is 96.
The count is last minus first, divided by 8, plus 1.
steps: The first multiple of 8, from 1 onwards, is 8.
The last multiple of 8, up to 101, is 96.
The count is 96 minus 8, divided by 8, plus 1. That equals 12.

PH3_EXT_G5_WS_01_015_02.q: A book has 300 pages. How many digits are used to number all the pages?
hints: Pages 1 to 9 use 1 digit each, pages 10 to 99 use 2 digits each, and pages from 100 onwards use 3 digits each.
Count each group separately and add.
There are 9 single-digit pages.
steps: Pages 1 to 9: that is 9 pages, times 1 digit, which is 9 digits.
Pages 10 to 99: that is 90 pages, times 2 digits, which is 180.
Pages 100 to 300: that is 201 pages, times 3 digits, which is 603.
The total is 792 digits.

PH3_EXT_G5_WS_01_015_03.q: How many 4-digit numbers are there in all?
hints: The smallest 4-digit number is 1000 and the largest is 9999. You need to count every number from one to the other.
